## Use dataset built-in in R

## Categorical and a continuous variable

```{r}
data("iris")
head(iris)
mean(iris$Petal.Length)
table(iris$Species)
by(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Species, mean)
boxplot(Sepal.Length ~ Species, data = iris, main =  "Sepal Length by Species", xlab = "Species", ylab = "Sepal Length")
```
##Relationship btn two Categorical variable
```{r}

data("UCBAdmissions")
ucba<- data.frame(UCBAdmissions)
head(ucba)
cross<- xtabs(Freq~Gender+Admit,data=ucba) ## here you need to put cross to get the result
(cross<- xtabs(Freq~Gender+Admit,data=ucba))
prop.table(cross,2)

```
##Simpson's paradox
```{r}
cross2<-xtabs(Freq~Gender+Admit,data=ucba[ucba$Dept=="F",])
prop.table(cross2,1)
```

## Import Data and do Scatter plot
```{r}
data_class2<-read.table("C:\\Users\\HP\\Desktop\\Study\\Tasks\\height_weight_data.txt", header = TRUE)
```

## Subset (selecting variables,dropping variables,selecting observation )

```{r}
newdata3<-leadership[,c(5:9)]
myvars<-c("q1","q2","q3","q4","q5")
(newdata3<-leadership[myvars])
```
```{r}
newdata4<-leadership[,c(-1,-2)]
(newdata4<-leadership[,-(1:5)])
newdata5<-leadership[,c(-1,-7)]
leadership[[4]]

```

## Subsetting

```{r}
manager <- c(1,2,3,4,5)
country<- c("US","US","UK","UK","UK")
gender<-c("M","F","F","M","F")
age<-c(32,45,25,39,99)
q1<-c(5,3,3,3,2)
q2<-c(4,5,5,3,2)
q3<-c(5,2,5,4,1)
q4<-c(5,5,5,NA,2)
q5<-c(5,5,2,NA,1)
leadership<-data.frame(manager,country, gender, age, q1,q2,q3,q4,q5, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
leadership<-data.frame(manager,country, gender, age, q1,q2,q3,q4,q5)
str(leadership)

names(leadership)
leadership$age[leadership$age==99]<-NA
View(leadership)
leadership$agecat[leadership$age >75]<-"Elder"
leadership$agecat[leadership$age>=35 & leadership$age<=75]<-"Middle Aged"
leadership$agecat[leadership$age <35]<- "Young"
is.na(leadership[,5:9])
newdata<-na.omit(leadership)
newdata
```
